criteria.statement: On a scratch fixture repo whose base clashes with the branch in a file graded mechanical (and in no behavioural or forbidden file), `merge-resolve.js start` leaves a real merge in progress (`MERGE_HEAD` present), with conflict markers in the mechanical files only, and returns the list of those files
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 9: "runs a real `git merge --no-ff --no-commit` ... Mechanical: leaves the merge in progress with markers in only the mechanical files ... and returns the file list"; line 7: "when the base clashes beyond record files"
criteria.evidence: Transcript of `node .claude/lib/merge-resolve.js start --base origin/<base> --branch B --pr-head SHA --trd none --state-dir D` showing the returned file list; `git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD` succeeding; `git grep -l "<<<<<<<"` listing exactly the returned files

criteria.statement: Every conflicted file `start` reports carries the class `conflict-classifier.js classify` gives that same file; `merge-resolve.js` applies the classifier's grade and stop rule rather than its own
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 9: "grades with `classify`, then `decide`"; line 5: "rebuilds: none — this change calls them and adds no grading logic"
criteria.evidence: Jest case in `packages/core/lib/merge-resolve.test.js` (or a fixture transcript) comparing each `{path, class}` from `start`/`entry` against `classify` called directly on the same three stages, passing

criteria.statement: When the clash also includes record files, `start` resolves those by the same union `record-files.js` produces, so no record file is left holding markers or returned for the model to edit
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 9: "Record-file clashes are unioned exactly as `record-files.js` does"
criteria.evidence: Fixture with a record file and a mechanical file both clashing: the record file's merged text equals what `record-files.js` produces for the same inputs and carries no markers; it is absent from the returned file list

criteria.statement: `start` refuses, without starting a merge, when the checked-out branch is not B, when the PR head SHA is not contained in the branch, or when the working tree is not clean — the same preconditions `record-files.js merge-base-in` applies
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 9: "same preconditions as `record-files.js merge-base-in` (branch, PR head contained, clean tree)"
criteria.evidence: Three fixture transcripts (wrong branch, uncontained PR head, dirty tree), each a refusal naming the failed precondition, with no `MERGE_HEAD` afterwards and HEAD unchanged

criteria.statement: `check` refuses while any mechanical file still holds conflict markers, and does not report `commit`
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 10: "`check --state-dir D`: refuses a file that still holds markers"
criteria.evidence: Fixture transcript: `check` run with one mechanical file left unresolved names that file in its refusal; outcome is not `commit`

criteria.statement: `check` refuses a file whose text outside the conflict hunks changed after `start` (the model edited more than the hunks), judged against the snapshot `start` took from the merged files on disk before any edit; editing only inside the hunks passes this guard
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 9: "saves, straight from the merged files on disk (before the model touches them), a snapshot of each file's text outside the hunks"; line 10: "refuses a file ... whose text outside the hunks changed (the model edited more than the hunks)"
criteria.evidence: Two fixture transcripts from the same `start`: (a) markers resolved and one line outside a hunk also edited — `check` refuses naming the file; (b) only hunk content edited — `check` passes the guard and goes on to run checks

criteria.statement: With markers resolved inside the hunks only, `check` runs lint, typecheck and the affected tests, reports which it ran and their results, and returns `commit` when all pass
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 10: "then runs lint, typecheck and the affected tests ... returns `commit`, `fix` or `stop`"
criteria.evidence: Fixture transcript of `check` whose output names the lint, typecheck and test runs, each passing, and the outcome `commit`

criteria.statement: The checks `check` runs are spawned with argument arrays (`spawnSync`), never as an interpolated shell string
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 10: "through `spawnSync` with argument arrays"
criteria.evidence: Read of `.claude/lib/merge-resolve.js` showing each check invoked by `spawnSync(cmd, [args...])` with no `shell: true`, `execSync` or `exec` of a built string; or a jest case asserting the same

criteria.statement: While fewer than two fix attempts have failed, a failing `check` returns `fix`; once checks have failed after two fix attempts, `check` returns `stop` with the STUCK text, and does not commit
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 10: "calls `decide` with `checksFailed` and the failed-attempt count; returns `commit`, `fix` or `stop` plus the STUCK text"; line 5: "`decide` (the two-attempt rule)"
criteria.evidence: Fixture where a check is made to fail: successive `check` transcripts showing `fix`, then `stop` with STUCK text after the second failed attempt; `git rev-parse HEAD` unchanged from before `start`

criteria.statement: `commit` refuses unless the last `check` passed (none run, or the last returned `fix` or `stop`), and makes no commit
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 11: "`commit --state-dir D`: only after a passing check"
criteria.evidence: Fixture transcripts: `commit` before any `check`, and after a failing `check`, each refused, HEAD unchanged

criteria.statement: After a passing `check`, `commit` stages the mechanical files, makes the merge commit with git's own merge message (`--no-edit`), and returns the new head, which is the branch's HEAD and has the base as a second parent
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 11: "`git add` of the mechanical files, `git commit --no-edit`; returns the new head"
criteria.evidence: Fixture transcript of `commit` printing a SHA equal to `git rev-parse HEAD`; `git rev-list --parents -n1 HEAD` showing two parents, one the base; `git status --porcelain` empty

criteria.statement: No `merge-resolve.js` subcommand pushes or force-pushes: across `start`, `check`, `commit`, `abort` and `entry`, on the resolved, refused and stopped paths, the fixture's remote branch ref does not move
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 11: "Never pushes and never forces"
criteria.evidence: Fixture with a bare remote: `git ls-remote origin B` identical before and after each path; read of the library showing no `push` invocation

criteria.statement: The merge contract (`packages/core/contracts/ship-primitive-merge.md`, and its `.claude/contracts/` copy) pushes the resolved merge with a plain `git push origin <branch>` after `commit`, with no `--force` or `--force-with-lease`
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 11: "the contract pushes with a plain `git push origin <branch>`"
criteria.evidence: `npx jest packages/core/contracts/ship-primitives.test.js` passing, plus a read of both contract copies showing the plain push line and no force flag

criteria.statement: A clash containing a file graded behavioural makes `start` abort the merge (no `MERGE_HEAD`, HEAD and working tree as before `start`) and return the STUCK text `stuckText` produces for that decision, naming the behavioural file(s), together with the resolution entry
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 9: "Forbidden or behavioural: aborts the merge, returns the STUCK text from `stuckText` and the resolution entry"; naming the files: domain-derived — a STUCK that ends a merge must say which files clashed or the owner cannot act on it
criteria.evidence: Fixture transcript of `start` printing STUCK text that equals `stuckText` output for the same graded set and contains each behavioural path; `git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD` failing; `git status --porcelain` empty

criteria.statement: A clash containing a forbidden file makes `start` abort the merge and return the `stuckText` STUCK text naming the forbidden file(s), with the resolution entry, exactly as for a behavioural file
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 9: "Forbidden or behavioural: aborts the merge ..."; line 5: "the forbidden-path rules"; naming the files: domain-derived, as FS-14
criteria.evidence: Fixture transcript as FS-14 with a forbidden-path file in the clash

criteria.statement: When a behavioural or forbidden file clashes beside mechanical files, the whole merge is aborted; none of the mechanical files is left for resolution
criteria.cites: domain-derived: resolving the mechanical half while a behavioural or forbidden file stays unmerged would commit a partly merged base; source line 9 places the abort on the graded clash as a whole ("grades with `classify`, then `decide`. ... Forbidden or behavioural: aborts the merge")
criteria.evidence: Fixture transcript of `start` on a mixed clash: STUCK text, no `MERGE_HEAD`, empty returned file list

criteria.statement: `abort --state-dir D` ends an in-progress merge left by `start`: afterwards there is no `MERGE_HEAD`, HEAD is the pre-merge commit and the working tree is clean
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 12: "`abort --state-dir D` ... abort the merge"
criteria.evidence: Fixture transcript of `abort` after a mechanical `start`; `git rev-parse HEAD` equal to the pre-`start` SHA; `git status --porcelain` empty

criteria.statement: For a resolved merge, `entry` prints a ship-record entry with `files` (each `{path, class}`), `checks` (the checks run), `reproofScope`, `failedAttempts` and `outcome`, matching what happened
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 12: "print the ship-record entry (`{ files: [{path, class}], checks, reproofScope, failedAttempts, outcome }`)"
criteria.evidence: Fixture transcript of `entry` after a resolved run: JSON with all five keys, files matching FS-1, checks matching FS-7, `failedAttempts` equal to the failed checks counted before the pass

criteria.statement: For a stopped run, `entry` prints the same five keys: after a behavioural or forbidden abort it lists the stopping files and their class, and after the two-attempt stop `failedAttempts` is 2 and `outcome` records the stop
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 12 (entry shape); line 9: "returns ... the resolution entry" on the abort path
criteria.evidence: Fixture transcripts of `entry` after the FS-14 and FS-9 paths, each JSON with all five keys and the stop recorded

criteria.statement: The merge contract passes the `entry` output as `data.resolution` of the merge step's result, so every resolution, resolved or stopped, reaches the ship record
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 12: "the contract passes as `data.resolution` of the step's result"
criteria.evidence: `npx jest packages/core/contracts/ship-primitives.test.js packages/core/lib/ship-build.seam.test.js` passing, plus a read of `ship-primitive-merge.md` (both copies) showing `data.resolution` set from `entry` on both the resolved and stopped paths

criteria.statement: The vendored copies match their sources: `.claude/lib/merge-resolve.js` is identical to `packages/core/lib/merge-resolve.js`, and `.claude/contracts/ship-primitive-merge.md` to `packages/core/contracts/ship-primitive-merge.md`
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 3: "`.claude/lib/merge-resolve.js` copy", "`packages/core/contracts/ship-primitive-merge.md`, `.claude/contracts/ship-primitive-merge.md`"
criteria.evidence: `cmp` (or `diff`) of each pair exiting 0

criteria.statement: The new and changed jest suites pass: `packages/core/lib/merge-resolve.test.js`, `packages/core/contracts/ship-primitives.test.js`, and `packages/core/lib/ship-build.seam.test.js` including its added seam case
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 3: "`packages/core/lib/merge-resolve.test.js` new ... `packages/core/contracts/ship-primitives.test.js`) plus one added seam case in `packages/core/lib/ship-build.seam.test.js`"
criteria.evidence: Transcript of `npx jest packages/core/lib/merge-resolve.test.js packages/core/contracts/ship-primitives.test.js packages/core/lib/ship-build.seam.test.js` ending with all tests passed
